To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N-termini of AQP6 from mice and humans bind calmodulin in vitro and this binding activity is dependent on the presence of Ca(2+).
the N-termini of AQP6 bind to calmodulin in the presence of Ca2+ in a manner similar to other calmodulin target proteins.
AQP6 binds calmoduline in a calcium-dependent fashion and the calmodulin binding domain has been identified.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a novel AQP6/calmodulin complex.
understanding the role of calmodulin in regulating AQP6 anionic permeability.
the identification of the calmodulin binding sites in the N-termini of mouse and human AQP-6.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
calmodulin binding to the N-terminal of AQP6 is calcium dependent.
AQP6 is an anion selective channel, that is expressed in the kidney collecting duct, that is regulated by calmodulin binding, and that is gated by low intracellular pH.
AQP6 binds to calmodulin in the presence of Ca2+ in a calcium-dependent and pH-independent manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a novel calcium/calmodulin binding site on the N-termini of AQP6 that binds calcium/calmodulin in a concentration-dependent manner.
AQP6 binds calmodin with high affinity and that binding is dependent on calcium.
we identified a calcium-dependent binding site on the N-termini of AQP6 for calmodulin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AQP6 binds calmodulins in a calcium-dependent fashion.
we have demonstrated that AQP6 binds calmodin in the presence of Ca2+.
AQP6 is a calmodulin-binding protein.
